prompt:
Style: abstract-gouache. Transform the supplied ORIGINAL photograph of a LEGO Millennium Falcon model on a white cabinet, minifigures, a display plaque and nearby autumn foliage. Render only a single full-frame artwork using this style treatment:

- **artwork — selection.** An entirely new, highly abstract visual translation using the same photo as the sole visual source. Do not trace the scene, reconstruct the complete scene, or apply a conventional illustration filter. Identify the most recognizable subject, gesture, relationship, silhouette, structure, direction, or memory point, and select one defining feature — adapted by subject type (portraits: head contours, hairstyle direction, shoulder lines, profiles; actions: gesture direction, movement, balance; relationships: number, relative positions, contact points, interactions; architecture: rooflines, arches, towers, steps, proportions; landscapes: mountain contours, tree silhouettes, coastlines, horizons, water flow; animals: ears, head shapes, tails, wings, postures; everyday objects: outlines, handles, curves, structural features). - **artwork — composition.** The motif is centered or slightly off-center and occupies roughly 25–40% of the artwork's visual area, surrounded by generous clean negative space; it is not enlarged to fill the artwork. The background is warm ivory, soft off-white, or pale beige, with no prominent texture. - **Palette.** 3–5 muted colors chosen independently for each photo, based on its recognizable subject colors, light–dark contrasts, and emotional atmosphere, reinterpreted as soft modernist gouache tones. Never a fixed palette, never colors reused from another photo. - **Painted aesthetic.** Minimal hand-painted gouache with subtle paper-collage qualities — flat, matte, soft, slightly translucent color shapes, gently irregular edges, delicate hand-painted marks, subtle pigment variation, and minimal overlapping brushstrokes. Avoid strong grain, realistic paper fibers, heavy oil-paint textures, complex gradients, volumetric shadows, embossing, sculptural 3D paper layers, detailed outlines, and photographic textures. - **Abstraction limits.** The result must remain highly abstract — not a complete character sketch, cartoon, architectural line drawing, realistic watercolor, complex collage, or decorative pattern. - **Intended contrast.** Richly detailed reality above versus quiet, minimalist abstraction below. 

Preserve the original scene's subject relationships. Every part of the canvas must belong to the transformed artwork. No original photo panel, no before/after comparison, no split, no text.
